passages.text: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted. The horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.
passages.sermon:
Moses led the Israelites.
The Israelites had just escaped from Egypt.
The LORD had saved them from the Egyptians.
Moses and the Israelites sang a song to the LORD.
They said, “I will sing to the LORD.
The LORD is highly exalted.
He has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea.”
passages.original: אָ֣ז יָשִֽׁיר־ מֹשֶׁה֩ וּבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־ הַשִּׁירָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אָשִׁ֤ירָה לַֽיהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ גָאֹ֣ה גָּאָ֔ה ס֥וּס וְרֹכְב֖וֹ רָמָ֥ה בַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise Him, my father’s God, and I will exalt Him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is my strength.
The LORD is my song.
The LORD has become my salvation.
The LORD is my God.
I will praise Him.
The LORD is my father’s God.
I will exalt Him.
passages.original: עָזִּ֤י וְזִמְרָת֙ יָ֔הּ וַֽיְהִי־ לִ֖י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה זֶ֤ה אֵלִי֙ וְאַנְוֵ֔הוּ אֱלֹהֵ֥י אָבִ֖י וַאֲרֹמְמֶֽנְהוּ׃

passages.text: The LORD is a warrior, the LORD is His name.
passages.sermon: The LORD is a warrior.\r\nThe LORD is His name.
passages.original: יְהוָ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֑ה יְהוָ֖ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Pharaoh’s chariots and army He has cast into the sea; the finest of his officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is powerful.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh had chariots and an army.
The LORD threw Pharaoh’s chariots and army into the sea.
The Red Sea is where this happened.
The LORD drowned Pharaoh’s best officers in the Red Sea.
passages.original: מַרְכְּבֹ֥ת פַּרְעֹ֛ה וְחֵיל֖וֹ יָרָ֣ה בַיָּ֑ם וּמִבְחַ֥ר שָֽׁלִשָׁ֖יו טֻבְּע֥וּ בְיַם־ סֽוּף׃

passages.text: The depths have covered them; they sank there like a stone.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is a warrior.
The LORD is His name.
He cast Pharaoh’s chariots and army into the sea.
He drowned the finest of Pharaoh’s officers in the Red Sea.
The deep waters covered them.
They sank in the depths like a stone.
passages.original: תְּהֹמֹ֖ת יְכַסְיֻ֑מוּ יָרְד֥וּ בִמְצוֹלֹ֖ת כְּמוֹ־ אָֽבֶן׃

passages.text: Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has shattered the enemy.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD uses His right hand.
His right hand is majestic.
His right hand shows great strength.
The LORD’s right hand destroys the enemy.
The LORD’s right hand shatters those who oppose Him.
passages.original: יְמִֽינְךָ֣ יְהוָ֔ה נֶאְדָּרִ֖י בַּכֹּ֑חַ יְמִֽינְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה תִּרְעַ֥ץ אוֹיֵֽב׃

passages.text: You overthrew Your adversaries by Your great majesty. You unleashed Your burning wrath; it consumed them like stubble.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is powerful and majestic.
The Lord has great majesty.
The Lord overthrew His adversaries.
The Lord sent out His burning wrath.
His wrath consumed His enemies like stubble.
passages.original: וּבְרֹ֥ב גְּאוֹנְךָ֖ תַּהֲרֹ֣ס קָמֶ֑יךָ תְּשַׁלַּח֙ חֲרֹ֣נְךָ֔ יֹאכְלֵ֖מוֹ כַּקַּֽשׁ׃

passages.text: At the blast of Your nostrils the waters piled up; like a wall the currents stood firm; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted with great power.
God sent out a blast from His nostrils.
The waters piled up.
The flowing currents stood firm like a wall.
The deep waters became solid in the middle of the sea.
passages.original: וּבְר֤וּחַ אַפֶּ֙יךָ֙ נֶ֣עֶרְמוּ מַ֔יִם נִצְּב֥וּ כְמוֹ־ נֵ֖ד נֹזְלִ֑ים קָֽפְא֥וּ תְהֹמֹ֖ת בְּלֶב־ יָֽם׃

passages.text: The enemy declared, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword; my hand will destroy them.’
passages.sermon:
The enemy spoke.
The enemy said, "I will pursue."
The enemy said, "I will overtake."
The enemy said, "I will divide the spoils."
The enemy said, "I will fill myself with them."
The enemy said, "I will draw my sword."
The enemy said, "My hand will destroy them."
passages.original: אָמַ֥ר אוֹיֵ֛ב אֶרְדֹּ֥ף אַשִּׂ֖יג אֲחַלֵּ֣ק שָׁלָ֑ל תִּמְלָאֵ֣מוֹ נַפְשִׁ֔י אָרִ֣יק חַרְבִּ֔י תּוֹרִישֵׁ֖מוֹ יָדִֽי׃

passages.text: But You blew with Your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God blew with His breath.
The sea covered the enemy.
The enemy sank quickly.
They sank like lead.
They went down in the mighty waters.
passages.original: נָשַׁ֥פְתָּ בְרוּחֲךָ֖ כִּסָּ֣מוֹ יָ֑ם צָֽלֲלוּ֙ כַּֽעוֹפֶ֔רֶת בְּמַ֖יִם אַדִּירִֽים׃

passages.text: Who among the gods is like You, O LORD? Who is like You—majestic in holiness, revered with praises, performing wonders?
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is holy.
The LORD is majestic in holiness.
No other god is like the LORD.
No one is like the LORD among all gods.
People praise the LORD with awe.
The LORD does wonderful things.
The LORD performs miracles.
passages.original: מִֽי־ כָמֹ֤כָה בָּֽאֵלִם֙ יְהוָ֔ה מִ֥י כָּמֹ֖כָה נֶאְדָּ֣ר בַּקֹּ֑דֶשׁ נוֹרָ֥א תְהִלֹּ֖ת עֹ֥שֵׂה פֶֽלֶא׃

passages.text: You stretched out Your right hand, and the earth swallowed them up.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God stretched out His right hand.
The earth swallowed the enemies.
passages.original: נָטִ֙יתָ֙ יְמִ֣ינְךָ֔ תִּבְלָעֵ֖מוֹ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: With loving devotion You will lead the people You have redeemed; with Your strength You will guide them to Your holy dwelling.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is loving and powerful.
The LORD redeemed His people.
The LORD leads His redeemed people with loving devotion.
The LORD uses His strength to guide them.
The LORD guides His people to His holy dwelling.
passages.original: נָחִ֥יתָ בְחַסְדְּךָ֖ עַם־ ז֣וּ גָּאָ֑לְתָּ נֵהַ֥לְתָּ בְעָזְּךָ֖ אֶל־ נְוֵ֥ה קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the dwellers of Philistia.
passages.sermon: The nations will hear.\r\nThe nations will tremble.\r\nAnguish will grip the people who live in Philistia.
passages.original: שָֽׁמְע֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים יִרְגָּז֑וּן חִ֣יל אָחַ֔ז יֹשְׁבֵ֖י פְּלָֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: Then the chiefs of Edom will be dismayed; trembling will seize the leaders of Moab; those who dwell in Canaan will melt away, and terror and dread will fall on them. By the power of Your arm they will be as still as a stone until Your people pass by, O LORD, until the people You have bought pass by.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful and protects His people.
The chiefs of Edom will be dismayed.
The leaders of Moab will tremble.
All who live in Canaan will melt away.
Terror and dread will fall on them.
Your strong arm, O God, will make them as still as stone.
They will remain still until Your people pass by, O LORD.
They will remain still until the people You have redeemed pass by.
passages.original: אָ֤ז נִבְהֲלוּ֙ אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֔וֹם אֵילֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב יֹֽאחֲזֵ֖מוֹ רָ֑עַד נָמֹ֕גוּ כֹּ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י כְנָֽעַן׃ תִּפֹּ֨ל עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם אֵימָ֙תָה֙ וָפַ֔חַד בִּגְדֹ֥ל זְרוֹעֲךָ֖ יִדְּמ֣וּ כָּאָ֑בֶן עַד־ יַעֲבֹ֤ר עַמְּךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה עַֽד־ יַעֲבֹ֖ר עַם־ ז֥וּ קָנִֽיתָ׃

passages.text: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance— the place, O LORD, You have prepared for Your dwelling, the sanctuary, O Lord, Your hands have established.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has saved His people from Egypt.
The LORD will bring His people into a new land.
The LORD will plant His people on the mountain He owns.
This mountain is the LORD’s inheritance.
The LORD has prepared a place for Himself to live.
The LORD has made this place with His own hands.
This place is the LORD’s holy sanctuary.
passages.original: תְּבִאֵ֗מוֹ וְתִטָּעֵ֙מוֹ֙ בְּהַ֣ר נַחֲלָֽתְךָ֔ מָכ֧וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ פָּעַ֖לְתָּ יְהוָ֑ה מִקְּדָ֕שׁ אֲדֹנָ֖י כּוֹנְנ֥וּ יָדֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: The LORD will reign forever and ever!”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD rules over all things.
The LORD will always reign.
The LORD will never stop reigning.
The LORD’s rule lasts forever and ever.
passages.original: יְהוָ֥ה׀ יִמְלֹ֖ךְ לְעֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

passages.text: For when Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh had horses.
Pharaoh had chariots.
Pharaoh had horsemen.
Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea.
The LORD is God.
The LORD brought the waters of the sea back over Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen.
The Israelites are God’s people.
The Israelites walked through the sea.
The Israelites walked on dry ground.
passages.original: כִּ֣י בָא֩ ס֨וּס פַּרְעֹ֜ה בְּרִכְבּ֤וֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו֙ בַּיָּ֔ם וַיָּ֧שֶׁב יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵהֶ֖ם אֶת־ מֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָלְכ֥וּ בַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her with tambourines and dancing.
passages.sermon:
Miriam was a prophetess.
She was Aaron’s sister.
Miriam took a tambourine in her hand.
All the women followed Miriam.
The women had tambourines.
The women danced.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּח֩ מִרְיָ֨ם הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה אֲח֧וֹת אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־ הַתֹּ֖ף בְּיָדָ֑הּ וַתֵּצֶ֤אןָ כָֽל־ הַנָּשִׁים֙ אַחֲרֶ֔יהָ בְּתֻפִּ֖ים וּבִמְחֹלֹֽת׃

passages.text: And Miriam sang back to them: “Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; the horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.”
passages.sermon:
Miriam was a prophetess.
She was Aaron’s sister.
Miriam sang to the people.
She said, “Sing to the LORD.”
The LORD is highly exalted.
He threw the horse and its rider into the sea.
passages.original: וַתַּ֥עַן לָהֶ֖ם מִרְיָ֑ם שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ גָאֹ֣ה גָּאָ֔ה ס֥וּס וְרֹכְב֖וֹ רָמָ֥ה בַיָּֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Desert of Shur. For three days they walked in the desert without finding water.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses led the people of Israel away from the Red Sea.
The people of Israel entered the Desert of Shur.
They walked in the desert for three days.
They did not find any water.
passages.original: וַיַּסַּ֨ע מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִיַּם־ ס֔וּף וַיֵּצְא֖וּ אֶל־ מִדְבַּר־ שׁ֑וּר וַיֵּלְכ֧וּ שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת־ יָמִ֛ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְלֹא־ מָ֥צְאוּ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink the water there because it was bitter. (That is why it was named Marah.)
passages.sermon:
The Israelites came to a place called Marah.
They found water at Marah.
They could not drink the water at Marah.
The water was bitter.
That is why the place was named Marah.
The name Marah means "bitter."
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ מָרָ֔תָה וְלֹ֣א יָֽכְל֗וּ לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת מַ֙יִם֙ מִמָּרָ֔ה כִּ֥י מָרִ֖ים הֵ֑ם עַל־ כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־ שְׁמָ֖הּ מָרָֽה׃

passages.text: So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What are we to drink?”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel traveled in the desert with Moses.
They could not find water.
The people complained to Moses.
They said, “What will we drink?”
passages.original: וַיִּלֹּ֧נוּ הָעָ֛ם עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹ֖ר מַה־ נִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a log. And when he cast it into the waters, they were sweetened. There the LORD made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them, saying, “If you will listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and pay attention to His commands, and keep all His statutes, then I will not bring on you any of the diseases I inflicted on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
The Israelites were in the wilderness.
They found water at Marah, but it was bitter.
The people could not drink the water.
Moses cried out to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD showed Moses a piece of wood.
Moses threw the wood into the water.
The water became sweet.
The LORD gave the people a rule and a law there.
The LORD tested the people there.
The LORD said, “Listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God.
Do what is right in His eyes.
Pay attention to His commands.
Keep all His statutes.
If you do these things, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians.
I am the LORD who heals you.”
passages.original: וַיִּצְעַ֣ק אֶל־ יְהוָ֗ה וַיּוֹרֵ֤הוּ יְהוָה֙ עֵ֔ץ וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ֙ אֶל־ הַמַּ֔יִם וַֽיִּמְתְּק֖וּ הַמָּ֑יִם שָׁ֣ם שָׂ֥ם ל֛וֹ חֹ֥ק וּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וְשָׁ֥ם נִסָּֽהוּ׃ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אִם־ שָׁמ֨וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַ֜ע לְק֣וֹל׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ וְהַיָּשָׁ֤ר בְּעֵינָיו֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְהַֽאֲזַנְתָּ֙ לְמִצְוֺתָ֔יו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֖ כָּל־ חֻקָּ֑יו כָּֽל־ הַמַּֽחֲלָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־ שַׂ֤מְתִּי בְמִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לֹא־ אָשִׂ֣ים עָלֶ֔יךָ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה רֹפְאֶֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites traveled together in the wilderness.
They came to a place called Elim.
Elim had twelve springs of water.
Elim also had seventy palm trees.
The Israelites camped there by the waters.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵילִ֔מָה וְשָׁ֗ם שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה עֵינֹ֥ת מַ֖יִם וְשִׁבְעִ֣ים תְּמָרִ֑ים וַיַּחֲנוּ־ שָׁ֖ם עַל־ הַמָּֽיִם׃
